exposure: Difficulty of labor during vaginal delivery
Reason for cesarean section (maternal preference vs. obstetric indication)
outcome: Recommendation for future birth method (vaginal or cesarean)
cohort: The study included 204 women, with a mean age of 42 +/- 7.6 years, all of whom had a history of both vaginal and cesarean delivery.
finding: Among women who had experienced both birth methods, 63.2% recommended vaginal delivery primarily due to postpartum comfort, while those recommending cesarean section cited easier labor and pain avoidance during vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Experiences with the mode of birth strongly influenced recommendations, as difficult vaginal labor significantly increased the recommendation for cesarean delivery (65.4% vs. 10.4% for easy labor), and women whose C-sections were for obstetric reasons were more likely to recommend vaginal birth than those who chose C-sections.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively from women after they had experienced both vaginal and cesarean deliveries.
